title: で draws a boundary: みんなで and 世界で一番
summary: で marks the limit inside which an action or a state holds: a place, a group, a number, a region. It works with adjectives too.

blocks.text: Besides noun / verb / adjective, Japanese grammar sorts words into **static** words (体言: nouns and noun-like things) and **active** words (用言: verbs, adjectives and noun + copula). Active words **change shape** in their final kana and can modify. Static words never change, but they take **particles and the copula**. A noun plus だ or です becomes an active unit: 綺麗だ can become 綺麗だった or 綺麗で.
So the three possible engines (verb, adjective, noun + copula) are all active words.

**に** says where something goes or where it is. **へ** says its direction. **で** says the **boundary within which** an action or state takes place. Usually that is a place, but it need not be. Because で modifies active words, it works with verbs *and* with adjectives.

blocks.jp: この町で一番おいしいラーメン
blocks.en: The tastiest ramen in this town. (the boundary of the comparison)

blocks.jp: 世界で一番有名な歌手
blocks.en: The most famous singer in the world.

blocks.text: Numbers and groups are boundaries too

二人で踊る ("two of us dance"), 一人で行く ("go alone"), みんなで歌う ("we all sing"). The number or group is the limit of those who do it, just as a room is the limit of where. This is why one particle covers "where", "how many people" and "within what range".
で vs の with an adjective

世界の一番おいしいラーメン is possible: の links 世界 to the noun ラーメン, "the world's tastiest ramen". But in このラーメンは世界で一番おいしい you need で, because 世界 must modify the adjective おいしい, and の can only modify a noun that comes after it. (Modifiers always go before what they modify.)

items: Static words (nouns) take particles; active words (verb, adjective, noun + copula) change shape.
**で** marks the boundary of an action or state: place, group, number, range.
**の** modifies a noun; **で** modifies an active word.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: この町＿＿一番高いビルは駅の近くだ。
questions.note: で sets the boundary of the comparison and modifies the adjective 高い.
questions.en: The tallest building in this town is near the station.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 日本＿＿一番長い川はどれですか。
questions.note: Nで一番: the most … within N.
questions.en: Which is the longest river in Japan?

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 友達と二人＿＿ご飯を食べた。
questions.note: The number is the limit of who did it, so it takes で.
questions.en: Two of us (a friend and I) ate a meal.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.note: で marks the boundary within which the action happened.
questions.en: I waited for my friend in front of the station.

questions.instruction: What does で mark?
options: The boundary within which an action or state takes place
Only the place something goes to
questions.note: A place, a group, a number or a range can all be boundaries.

questions.instruction: Why is で needed, not の?
questions.prompt: この店のカレーは町で一番安い。
options: 町 must modify the adjective 安い, and の can only modify a noun
questions.note: Modifiers of active words take で; の links to a noun.
questions.en: The curry at this shop is the cheapest in town.

questions.instruction: Which word is active (it changes shape)?
questions.note: Verbs, adjectives and noun + copula are active; plain nouns are static.

questions.instruction: Which words never change shape but take particles and the copula?
questions.note: Static words take particles; active words change their final kana.

questions.instruction: What turns the noun 学生 into an active unit?
questions.note: A noun + だ or です becomes an engine that can change shape.

questions.instruction: What does で mark here?
questions.note: A number or group is the limit of those who do it.

questions.instruction: True or false: で and へ both say the direction of movement.
questions.note: へ says direction; で says the boundary of an action or state.

questions.instruction: True or false: の can modify an adjective such as おいしい.
questions.note: の can only modify a noun that comes after it.

questions.instruction: Which particle says where something is or goes?
questions.note: に marks where something goes or is; で marks the boundary of an action.

questions.instruction: Which sentence is NOT natural?
options: このカレーは日本で一番おいしい。
このカレーは日本の一番おいしい。
日本で一番おいしいカレー
日本の一番おいしいカレー
questions.note: To modify the adjective おいしい you need で; の only links nouns.

questions.instruction: What does the で in Nで一番 give?
questions.note: Nで一番 = the most … within N.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that sets the boundary of the comparison
questions.note: 町で is the range inside which ビル is the tallest.
questions.en: I saw the tallest building in this town.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that gives the limit of who did it
questions.note: で marks the number as the boundary.
questions.en: I watched a movie with a friend, just the two of us.

questions.instruction: Tap the engine that で modifies
questions.note: で and を both modify the engine 待った.
questions.en: I waited for a friend in front of the station.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: the cheapest store in this town
questions.note: で modifies the adjective; modifiers come before the noun.
questions.en: The cheapest store in this town.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I went on a trip with my friend, just the two of us.
questions.note: で marks the number; the engine comes last.
questions.en: I went on a trip with my friend, just the two of us.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I played with my dog in the park.
questions.note: で gives the place boundary of 遊んだ.
questions.en: I played with my dog in the park.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: This curry is the tastiest in Japan.
questions.note: 日本で modifies おいしい.
questions.en: This curry is the tastiest in Japan.
